parallel.requirements: Recognized Rust 2021, no external crates, `std::env::args()`, byte-for-byte stdout with trailing spaces, black-box inference from the compiled C++ binary, and required Cargo project plus root `/output/test1.rs`.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but spawned pattern_probe and layout_check to derive/verify behavior. The children also performed implementation writes, creating overlapping ownership of the shared output and entry file.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented a `src`-module Cargo project and root `test1.rs`; pattern_probe independently implemented another `src` project; layout_check independently implemented a root-module project. All targeted the same deterministic ear-clipping order and `atoi` behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parallel workspace ended with evidence of mixed root-level and `src` artifacts from multiple agents. Pattern_probe attempted reconciliation by changing root files and deleting `src` files, while the parent final still described the earlier `src` project.
parallel.verification: The parent verified Cargo and standalone builds against the oracle for n=1..20 plus edge args before child reconciliation; layout_check verified its root package; pattern_probe later saw cargo/rustc failures after the mixed-tree patch.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator completed but marked the solution false at 38/39. The parallel process also left stale verification relative to later child edits and a child-observed temporary broken package state.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, no-dependency, `std::env::args()`, byte-for-byte output, black-box oracle, Cargo project, and root `/output/test1.rs` obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the full pipeline: inspect oracle behavior, initialize Cargo, replace scaffold with modules and root entry, build, verify, and deliver.
serial.implementation: Created a coherent Cargo project with `Cargo.toml`, root `test1.rs`, and `src/args.rs`, `src/geometry.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, and `src/triangulation.rs`, implementing the inferred linked-list ear-clipping order.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final workspace was a single coherent `src`-based layout with no cross-agent writes or competing package roots. The final response matched the artifact layout.
serial.verification: After Python was unavailable, the serial run used shell comparisons and verified the executable against the C++ oracle for n=1..50 plus checked `atoi`-style edge cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also failed one hidden testcase, giving 38/39 and solution_passed false; no serial coordination issue is implicated.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial are solution_passed false with 38 of 39 testcases passed. The parallel run has a directly evidenced shared-output overwrite episode, but because the serial run also failed one official testcase, that episode is recorded as adverse process instability rather than a pass/fail outcome explanation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used multiple live agents that wrote competing implementations and the required `/output/test1.rs` deliverable in the same workspace.
Parent verification was stale relative to a later child reconciliation attempt that deleted `src` files and observed cargo/rustc failures.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one coherent project layout and verified the final delivered executable after building it.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations likely shared an ordinary hidden-case defect not isolated by the available trajectories, because both official outcomes are 38/39.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator completed normally in both modes and reports the same pass rate; no evaluator failure is evident.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel_adverse_but_not_outcome_differential

candidates.reason: The parent and children all undertook implementation work; the problem was overlapping ownership and writes, not absence of an implementation owner.
The parent retained final integration/closure authority and children also wrote complete packages; the concrete failure boundary is shared deliverable writes.
The root entry and package assembly were actively produced by multiple agents, so assembly was not ownerless; it was over-owned in the shared output tree.
The parent executed probing, implementation, build, verification, and closure; there was an end-to-end owner even though concurrent writes undermined state consistency.
Oracle probing occurred, but implementation proceeded in overlapping parent and child work; productive work was not blocked behind one serial gate with a qualifying delay consequence.
Investigation and implementation overlapped across parent and children; the adverse episode was competing writes, not a separate investigation phase delaying all implementation.
The implementation path had active parent and child capacity and produced builds; no indispensable path was starved of workers apart from the write conflict.
Only two children were spawned and the parent completed within budget; timeouts occurred but did not collectively exhaust the run before implementation/verification.
No single child received an overbroad indispensable assignment whose scope caused unfinished work; child issues stemmed from shared-state conflict and interruption.
The available child behavior shows awareness of the same task, oracle, Cargo, and root entry obligations; the defect was not a missing requirement in the initial child brief.
There was no merely abstract interface mismatch between separate components; live agents concretely replaced the same deliverable and package files, so the write label is more specific.
No known finding or current-file fact is shown disappearing in transfer; the conflict was visible through shared files rather than missing handoff content.
No returned result was too large or poorly structured to consume; the parent did not fail because it could not reduce an oversized handoff.
Although parent verification became stale relative to later writes, the stale state came from concurrent workspace mutation, not consumption of a superseded handoff.
The incompatible information did not arrive as unadjudicated reports; it materialized as direct competing file writes, which the taxonomy classifies under concurrent writes.
The parent did perform integrated local checks before finalizing; the hidden official 1/39 failure alone cannot establish unsupported completion under this taxonomy.
No replacement retry without inherited findings is shown; the children were initial parallel actors, not checkpoint-free retries repeating failed work.

candidates.reason: Children were interrupted, but the directly corrective boundary for the same chain is preventing the shared deliverable overwrite; retaining termination would duplicate the downstream symptom.
A directly promotable compatible candidate set was not simply left unplaced; multiple candidates collided in the final workspace and the parent did produce a deliverable.
There were later child edits after parent verification, but the material event was an overwrite of the required deliverable rather than a legitimate result merge after checks.
The children did not merely complete retrievable implementations that the parent failed to join; their implementations directly wrote into and conflicted within the shared `/output` tree.
No verifier child produced a trapped finding that failed to return; child outputs were implementation artifacts and shared-state changes, not unreturned verifier results.
Pattern_probe's later failures were downstream of the conflicting file rewrite, and the parent had already produced a candidate implementation; this is not a separate required child failure takeover.
No concise completed child result was returned to the parent and then ignored at a decision point; the notable child effects were direct shared-file writes.
The parent waited and timed out, but it also inspected/listed children and proceeded after its own verification; the realized harm is better captured by the shared deliverable overwrite.
The episode includes same deliverable replacement, so the less specific cross-file overlap label is superseded by Deliverable Overwrite.
The same required entry file was involved, but because it was the directly executed/submitted `/output/test1.rs` deliverable, the taxonomy precedence selects Deliverable Overwrite.
Non-entry source files were also changed and deleted, but the required root executable entry source was overwritten, making Deliverable Overwrite more specific.

Multiple live parallel agents wrote the required `/output/test1.rs` entry deliverable and incompatible package roots in the shared output directory; one child then observed the conflict, deleted `src` files, and hit build failures, while serial used one coherent writer.
candidates.realized_consequence: Stale parent verification and a temporarily broken mixed workspace: the child reconciliation deleted `src` files expected by the parent package and cargo/rustc failed in that child.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is a near match, but `/output/test1.rs` is the required executable entry source, so deliverable overwrite is the more specific canonical label.

candidates.reason: The patch changed multiple files, but the defining object was the required root entry deliverable and its package layout, so Deliverable Overwrite has precedence.
The workspace was unisolated, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven; the generic unisolated label is therefore suppressed.
No generated auxiliary artifact or cache from one actor was consumed as stable reference input by another; the issue was direct source/deliverable replacement.

retained_patterns.reason: Separate live parallel actors wrote the same required `/output/test1.rs` deliverable and incompatible package layouts in shared `/output`; a child later observed the conflict, patched over files, deleted `src` modules, and saw build failures. The serial run wrote one coherent project tree.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Final-Tree Overwrite, and Unisolated Workspace Writes are suppressed because they describe the same shared `/output` write chain and Deliverable Overwrite is the most specific label.

Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Missing Implementation Join, Merge after Verification, and Blind Timeout Wait are not retained because their evidence is downstream or secondary to the same write-conflict episode.
